summary: Listed as a Pitt County tower on a statewide NC list (35.55611, -77.37111). The only Greenville tower sources describe is a 1940 city fire drill tower, not a lookout.

facts.design: Brick, concrete and steel training tower, 18 by 18 feet and 60 feet tall, with a concrete stairway to the roof (drill tower; match to the list entry not confirmed)

events.note: Photograph record dates the city fire drill tower on Chestnut Street to 1940; a note on the photograph says the Minges drill tower was donated to the fire department and city that year. A training tower, not a lookout.

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The list entry (tnlandforms, Pitt County) is a statewide lookout list. The only Greenville tower with evidence is the city's 1940 fire drill training tower on Chestnut Street (ECU photograph record). That is a training tower, not a forest lookout, and nothing we read ties the list coordinates to Chestnut Street; do not publish it as a lookout until the list entry is matched. The ECU record calls the donor's firm a 'Pespi-Cola' plant. A search snippet (not opened) gave a 1942 completion, an April 13, 1943 dedication and a Coca-Cola firm; no page we opened confirms those, so they are not used. A 1950 ECU item we opened was unrelated. Next checks: Greenville city records, ECU Joyner Library, NC Forest Service Pitt County office. No photos added: the ECU image URL and license were not confirmed.
